evidence_items.evidence_summary: MOF described the Jobs Support Scheme as wage support for employers, with payouts automatically computed based on CPF contribution data.
The Jobs Support Scheme was introduced in Budget 2020 to help enterprises retain local employees during the COVID-19 period of economic uncertainty.

evidence_items.source_title: Supporting Jobs and Livelihoods during the Pandemic
evidence_items.evidence_summary: JSS was introduced in the Unity Budget on 18 February 2020, initially providing wage support during a period of economic uncertainty.

evidence_items.source_title: Impact of the Jobs Support Scheme on Labour Market Outcomes
evidence_items.evidence_summary: Government analysis found that higher effective JSS wage subsidies were associated with better local wage outcomes, indicating labour market stabilization effects.

evidence_items.source_title: COVID-19 Economic Shock and Circuit Breaker Context
evidence_items.evidence_summary: The scheme operated during the COVID-19 downturn and circuit breaker period, meaning observed employment or business outcomes may also reflect demand shock and operational disruption.

mechanism_assessment.primary_mechanism: Government wage subsidies reduced employer labour cost pressure and supported worker retention during the COVID-19 downturn.
secondary_mechanisms: automatic payout design reduced application friction
CPF contribution data enabled targeted employer support
sectoral and broad-based support helped cushion labour market stress
policy support interacted with demand collapse and operational restrictions
transmission_chain: COVID-19 shock reduced business revenue and activity
government introduced wage support through JSS
employment and wage outcomes were partly stabilized

driver_evidence_summary.summary: The case is directly policy-native: JSS was a government wage support intervention designed to preserve jobs and business continuity.
The policy response was triggered by the COVID-19 economic downturn, so demand shock remains an important contextual driver.
Operational restrictions during the COVID period affected business activity, but this appears secondary to the policy-support mechanism.

evidence_assessment.notes: This evidence package supports classification of SG-JOBS-SUPPORT-SCHEME-2020 as a policy-native replay case with MKT_006 as the expected primary driver.
